headline: 🔴 SonicWall SMA1000 CVSS 10.0 SSRF exploited within a day of patch, 🕳️ Public PoC for AnyPwn AnyDesk pre-auth root RCE, 🏛️ FBI ties ShinyHunters FBIjobs breach to unpatched contractor PeopleSoft, 🎤 Nippon Columbia breach exposes 8.6M karaoke fans, 🔐 GitLab CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE, 📅 Let's Encrypt moves to 64-day certificates
summary: Honeypots confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of SonicWall's max-severity SMA1000 SSRF within a day of patching, while public PoC code landed for a pre-auth root RCE in AnyDesk for Linux. The FBI pinned its ShinyHunters breach on one missed patch on a contractor's PeopleSoft platform, GitLab and WuKong_HRM shipped CVSS-critical access flaws, and Let's Encrypt set the certificate ecosystem on a path to 64-day defaults.

overrides.why: Highest-scored evolved story (6.8, last covered Oct 10): today's SecurityWeek report plus Previdian/Defused honeypot telemetry confirm in-the-wild exploitation within a day of the Oct 6 patch, the day's defining operational development.
Below the 3.3 gate at 3.1 but the Oct 12 GBHackers follow-up adds kit detail on UAT-11985's AI-generated lures paired with live AitM MFA bypass, a novel TTP never covered in a digest.
All four post-Oct-11 events (qz.com, killbait x2, dailytechnow) are outlet re-reports of the 123456 disclosure already covered in yesterday's digest; no new facts.
The Oct 12 GBHackers and hacks.gr events re-tell the Oct 8 Bitdefender disclosure (same 150+ countries, ad fraud, proxy botnets) with no new devices, C2 or technical facts.
The Oct 12 securityonline.info event re-reports Zscaler's Oct 8 TraderTraitor/FLATROOF/ROOFDECK findings verbatim; covered Oct 9.
